name: Oregon State University

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted into House settlement (2025). Amount shared not verified; as a cash-strapped 'Pac-2' survivor it is believed to share well below the $20.5M (2025-26) cap. FY2024 revenue inflated by final legacy Pac-12 distributions/settlement money.
athletics.note: Revenue/expense figures are best-recall approximations of Knight-Newhouse/USA Today FY2024 data; not re-verified.

ratingNotes: FB: 2023 8-5 (Jonathan Smith left for Michigan State); 2024 5-7 under Trent Bray; 2025 very poor (believed 2-10 range) and coaching change — rated weak G6 entering the rebuilt Pac-12. MBB: Wayne Tinkle era, last NCAA trip 2021 Elite Eight; mid-pack in WCC as affiliate 2024-26. WBB: 2023-24 Elite Eight under Scott Rueck, solid since. Olympic: baseball is a national brand (3 CWS titles; 2025 CWS run as an independent, low confidence); Directors' Cup roughly top-75. Facilities: Reser west-side rebuild opened 2023. Political: Oregon legislature and governor engaged after the 2023 Pac-12 collapse.

headFootballCoach.name: JaMarcus Shephard
headFootballCoach.note: Recollection: Trent Bray (hired Dec 2023) dismissed during a winless 2025 start and replaced by Washington assistant JaMarcus Shephard; could not re-verify (search budget exhausted).

notes: One of the two 'Pac-2' schools left when ten members announced exits in 2023. With WSU sued the Pac-12 in Whitman County (Sept 2023) and won control of the board (WA Supreme Court declined review, Dec 2023); the pair kept conference assets, reserves and NCAA units, used the two-year NCAA grace period, played 2024-25 football with a Mountain West scheduling agreement (which carried the 'poaching penalty' clause) and parked most other sports in the WCC as affiliates. Rebuilt Pac-12 launched July 1, 2026 around them. Civil War vs Oregon continues as a non-conference game. Small Corvallis market (Eugene DMA; Portland is the alumni market). Oregon state funding/legislative attention is a lever in any future realignment. Wrestling is OSU's sport that anchors the Pac-12 wrestling affiliate structure.
note: Enrollment, endowment, US News rank and DMA rank are approximate (best recall; search budget exhausted). Corvallis is generally assigned to the Eugene DMA.

name: Washington State University

MBB: 2024 NCAA R32 (Kyle Smith left for Stanford); David Riley rebuilding. WBB: 2023 Pac-12 tournament champs. Olympic: Directors' Cup ~top-100. Fan base: 'Ol' Crimson' flag tradition, strong alumni loyalty, remote Pullman limits attendance.

notes: Co-plaintiff with Oregon State in the 2023 suit that gave the 'Pac-2' control of the Pac-12; litigation and settlement with the departing ten (incl. liability allocation for House damages) define the rebuilt league's balance sheet. Apple Cup vs Washington continues as a non-conference game. Pullman is a small, remote market (Spokane DMA shared with Gonzaga). Heavy leadership churn 2024-26 (president, AD, two football coaches). Washington legislature and the state AG were engaged in the Pac-12 fight; state politics matter for any further move.

name: Boise State University

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted into House settlement (2025); exact share not verified — among the more aggressive G6 sharers.

ratingNotes: FB: G6's premier program — 2007/2010(BCS)/2015 Fiesta wins; 2024 12-2, MWC champ, CFP No. 3 seed (first-round bye), lost Fiesta QF to Penn State; Ashton Jeanty Heisman runner-up. 2025 again a MWC contender (details not re-verified). Top-G6 = 45-50. MBB: Leon Rice, NCAA 2022-24, NIT 2025. Brand: blue turf, national TV draw for G6. Facilities: new football complex; ExtraMile Arena.
notes: Long the Mountain West's flagship; its 2012-13 Big East flirtation won it a special MWC deal (bonus TV share + right to sell its home football games separately). Announced Pac-12 move Sept 12, 2024 with Colorado State, Fresno State and San Diego State; central to the MWC exit-fee and 'poaching penalty' litigation with the Pac-12 (MWC sought exit fees from each departing school plus poaching fees owed by the Pac-12 under the 2024-25 OSU/WSU scheduling deal). Treasure Valley growth and Idaho legislature support. Perennial P4 expansion talking point (Big 12 in 2023-24).
note: Enrollment, endowment, US News, DMA rank approximate.

CSU System (Board of Governors) governance; Colorado politics relatively hands-off.

Part of the 23-campus CSU system — CSU budget cuts and chancellor/trustee oversight shape athletics spending; Central Valley legislators are vocal boosters. 2025 sports-betting scrutiny of Fresno State basketball players is an event-seed (low confidence on details).

name: San Diego State University

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted into House settlement (2025); amount not verified.

ratingNotes: FB: Rocky Long/Brady Hoke era consistency (2021 12-2); 2024 3-9 in Sean Lewis year 1, sharp rebound in 2025 (not re-verified). MBB: Brian Dutcher — 2023 national runner-up, 2024 Sweet 16, 2025 First Four; regular tournament team. Facilities: Snapdragon Stadium (2022) in Mission Valley development; Viejas Arena. Market: San Diego DMA top-30, the league's biggest single-school market.
notes: Original Pac-12 suitor: in June 2023 SDSU sent the MWC a letter about possibly leaving (widely read as pre-positioning for Pac-12/Big 12 expansion); the MWC treated it as a withdrawal notice, SDSU disputed, then reversed course — a template for exit-notice brinkmanship and withheld distributions. Joined the rebuild four in Sept 2024 for 2026. Mission Valley stadium deal with the City of San Diego; CSU system trustees and chancellor exert budget pressure. Oil Can vs Fresno State continues in-conference; UNLV basketball rivalry becomes non-conference.
note: Enrollment, endowment, US News, DMA rank approximate.

arena.name: Strahan Arena at the University Events Center

ratingNotes: FB: G.J. Kinne turned it around — 2023 first-ever bowl win, 2024 8-5 with second straight First Responder Bowl win; competitive 2025. MBB: occasional Sun Belt contender; last NCAA 1997. Facilities: stadium end-zone and indoor-practice investment. Political: Texas State University System and a Texas legislature that routinely weighs in on realignment.
notes: Last piece of the rebuild: the Pac-12 needed an eighth football school for FBS status once Gonzaga (non-football) was counted, and admitted Texas State on June 30, 2025 for 2026; its regents approved a ~$5M buyout of the Sun Belt. Gives the Pac-12 a Texas recruiting footprint and the fast-growing Austin-San Antonio corridor (~40,000 students). I-35 rivalry with UTSA (American) is now non-conference. Expect Texas legislators/TSUS chancellor to be vocal in any future move.
note: Enrollment, endowment, US News, DMA rank approximate. San Marcos (Hays County) is in the Austin DMA.

name: Gonzaga University

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted into House settlement (believed); sharing concentrated in men's and women's basketball. Private — not in the USA Today database; EADA-based estimate.
athletics.note: Revenue/expenses are rough EADA-style estimates; opt-in and amount not re-verified.

ratingNotes: No varsity football since 1941. MBB: Mark Few — NCAA every year since 1999, title games 2017 and 2021, nine-ish straight Sweet 16s to 2023, 2024 Sweet 16, 2025 R32; perennial top-4-seed caliber. WBB: Lisa Fortier, regular NCAA team (2024 Sweet 16). Brand: national basketball brand bigger than many P4 schools. Facilities: McCarthey ('The Kennel') small but sold out; Volkar Center (2022).
notes: Non-football full member — the Pac-12's basketball crown jewel and NCAA-unit engine. Seriously courted by the Big 12 (2023-24) and discussed by the Big East; chose the Pac-12 (announced Oct 2024) leaving the WCC after 2025-26. Private Jesuit school — low state-political exposure. Few succession is a looming event; Gonzaga could be a 'flight risk' to the Big East/Big 12 if the Pac-12 basketball product or media money disappoints.
note: Enrollment, endowment, US News rank approximate.
